paragraphs: In [Niddah 27a](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.27a.7) [supplied בנדה כג., 23a], R’ Avin bar Rav Adda speaks in the name of R’ Menachem of Kfar Sha’arayim (or, according to another reading, of Beit Sha’arayim): There was a case in which one fetus was delayed after its fellow by three months, and behold, they sit before us: Yehuda and Hizkiya (the sons of R’ Chiyya).

notes.text: The supplied locator is Niddah23a; the complete matching passage is Niddah27a, which also uses Rav Menachem where the notice has Rabbi. The quoted three-month interval and the sons’ names remain as the notice reports them.

No new primary scalar was supplied for this entry. The earlier Niddah27a match and RavMenachem versus Hyman’s abbreviated title are inherited; the supplied כג. (23a) remains visibly separate. Nested said-attributions, three months, Kfar/BeitShaarayim alternatives, and Hyman’s parenthetical sons-of-Chiyya remain. There is no new medical or chronological inference. This second pass does not claim a fresh whole-folio27a inspection or a newly proven nonmatch at23a.

Hyman’s print has Niddah 27a (כז.), while the supplied transcription has 23a (כג.). The consulted 27a names Rav Menachem and gives both Kfar and Beit Sha’arayim. It places Yehuda and Hizkiya in the study hall and names their father. Hyman gives the father in parentheses. The next paragraph contains Abaye’s explanation of the three-month interval.
